title: Mutable default arguments
code:
def add(item, items=[]):
    items.append(item)
    return items

add(1)
print(add(2))
answer: [1, 2] — the default list is created once and shared between calls.
explanation: Default values are evaluated once at function definition. Use `items=None` and create a new list inside the function.

title: list vs tuple
body: What is a key difference between a list and a tuple?

options.t: Tuples are immutable (and hashable if their items are), lists are mutable

explanation: Hashable tuples can be dictionary keys or set members; lists cannot.

title: The GIL
body: In standard CPython builds, what does the Global Interpreter Lock imply for CPU-bound code?

options.t: Threads run Python bytecode truly in parallel on all cores
Only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, so CPU-bound work should use multiprocessing (or native extensions)

options.e: Threads release the GIL during blocking I/O.

answer: One thread runs bytecode at a time.
explanation: Threads still help I/O-bound work. CPython 3.13 introduced an experimental free-threaded build without the GIL, but the default build keeps it.

title: Generators
body: What is the main advantage of a generator (a function using `yield`)?

options.t: It runs faster than any loop
It produces values lazily, one at a time, without building the whole sequence in memory
It can be indexed like a list

explanation: Generators are ideal for streaming large files or infinite sequences; they can be iterated only once.

title: List comprehension output
code: print([i * i for i in range(4) if i % 2 == 0])
explanation: range(4) yields 0..3; the filter keeps 0 and 2; their squares are 0 and 4.
